goal.text: Personal data of hospital staff and named patients protected

query.organization_type: medium-sized distributor with an order portal and an LLM-based ordering assistant

kpis.text: Personal data fields classified with a documented purpose (100%)
Patient identifiers stored outside named-patient order records (0)
Data subject requests closed (within the legal deadline)

beliefs: Named-patient orders contain a patient name and medical record number
constraints: Patient identifiers are not sent to the language model provider

ranked_patterns.relevance: Highest relevance: its IT goal 'Personal data minimized and classified' maps almost one-to-one onto G06-K1 (fields classified with a documented purpose, 100%) and supports G06-K2 (no identifiers outside named-patient order records). Its data inventory, masking and retention constraint transfer directly to the distributor's order portal, and its conflict resolution (keep aggregated history, delete identifiers) is the same tension that named-patient ordering creates.

Second: 'Data subject requests fulfilled' is the direct source for G06-K3 (requests closed within the legal deadline). Its register-and-verify / export-or-erase tasks, request register resource, DPO plus service-agent actors and identity-verification constraint are reusable once 'Customer Service Agent' is re-cast as the Sales Administrator serving hospital buyers and named patients.

Third: the query organization runs an LLM-based ordering assistant, and SKB-05/G3 governs exactly that risk class. Its constraint 'customer personal data is not sent to the model provider beyond the session' is the template for the query constraint on patient identifiers, and its change register / periodic AI risk review give the controls that keep G06-K2 at zero in the assistant.

Fourth and weakest for privacy content, but closest in domain: hospital pharmacy medicine handling. It contributes the regulated record-keeping belief (batch/traceability records are mandatory, which explains why patient identifiers must be kept inside the named-patient order record) and the 'only a pharmacist may release' authority constraint, adapted here to release of named-patient data.

elements.text: Maintain a data inventory that records, for every personal data field of the order portal and the ordering assistant, its purpose, legal basis, owner and retention period
elements.justification: Direct adaptation of 'Maintain a data inventory with purpose and retention per field'; it is the operation that produces the 100% classification measured by G06-K1 and covers both hospital staff accounts and named-patient fields.

elements.text: Mask or pseudonymise hospital staff and patient data in test, training and support copies of the order portal
elements.justification: Adapted from 'Mask personal data in non-production systems'; a field cannot be classified as purpose-limited if unmasked copies circulate outside production, so this task protects the credibility of G06-K1.

elements.text: Scan order portal databases, interface files, logs and assistant conversation transcripts for patient names and medical record numbers held outside the named-patient order record, and remove or relocate every finding
elements.justification: Minimization task derived from the pattern's data-minimization goal, re-targeted to the query belief that named-patient orders carry a patient name and medical record number; it is the detection mechanism behind the target of 0 for G06-K2.

elements.text: Redact patient identifiers from prompts, retrieval context and assistant logs before any call to the language model provider, and block the call when redaction fails
elements.justification: Operationalises the query constraint 'Patient identifiers are not sent to the language model provider', taken from the pattern constraint limiting customer personal data sent to the model provider; keeps assistant usage from creating identifier copies counted by G06-K2.

elements.text: Record every model, prompt or retrieval-source change of the ordering assistant in a change register and obtain approval from the AI Product Owner and the Data Protection Officer before release
elements.justification: Adapted from 'Keep a model and prompt change register'; without attributable change control a redaction rule can be silently removed, which would break both the query constraint and G06-K2.

elements.text: Review the privacy and AI risk assessment of the order portal and ordering assistant with the Data Protection Officer, IT Security Officer and Quality Assurance Officer on a fixed periodic cycle
elements.justification: Adapted from 'Review the AI risk assessment with the risk committee'; gives G06 a recurring control point covering all three KPIs without inventing a new target value.

elements.text: Register each data subject request from hospital staff or from a named patient and verify the requester's identity before acting on it
elements.justification: Direct adaptation of 'Register and verify each data subject request'; registration is what makes closure within the legal deadline measurable for G06-K3.

elements.text: Export, correct or erase the requester's personal data, taking account of records that regulation requires the distributor to keep, and close the request within the legal deadline
elements.justification: Adaptation of 'Export or erase the customer's data', qualified by the regulated-records belief of SKB-07/G2 so that erasure never conflicts with mandatory named-patient supply traceability.

elements.text: Data inventory of the order portal and ordering assistant (field, purpose, legal basis, retention, system owner)
elements.justification: The pattern's 'Data inventory' resource; it is the evidence base from which the 100% classification figure of G06-K1 is reported.

elements.text: Masking and pseudonymisation tool for non-production copies of portal data
elements.justification: The pattern's 'Masking tool', required to execute the masking task that keeps classified fields purpose-limited.

elements.text: Patient identifier exception report listing identifiers found outside named-patient order records, with age and resolution status
elements.justification: Adapted from the pattern's periodic exception reporting ('Report items expiring within 90 days'), re-purposed from expiring stock to stray identifiers so that deviations from the target of 0 in G06-K2 surface and are cleared.

elements.text: Data subject request register covering hospital staff and named patients, with receipt date, deadline and closure date
elements.justification: The pattern's 'Request register', the single source for measuring closure within the legal deadline in G06-K3.

elements.text: Model and prompt change register and AI privacy risk register for the ordering assistant
elements.justification: The pattern's 'Change register' and 'AI risk register', needed to make assistant changes attributable and to keep the no-identifiers-to-provider constraint auditable.

elements.text: Data Protection Officer
elements.justification: Present in both SKB-03 goals and in the query actor list; owns the data inventory, approves assistant changes that touch personal data and is accountable for the whole of G06.

elements.text: System Owner of the order portal (IT Security Officer acting as system owner for security controls)
elements.justification: The pattern's 'System Owner' mapped to the query's IT Security Officer; supplies the field-level purpose and retention entries and enforces masking, which drives G06-K1.

elements.text: Sales Administrator
elements.justification: The pattern's 'Customer Service Agent' re-cast to the query actor list; receives requests from hospital buyers and named patients, performs identity verification and executes the export or erasure.

elements.text: AI Product Owner
elements.justification: The pattern's 'AI Product Owner'; accountable for the redaction controls of the ordering assistant and therefore for preventing identifier copies counted in G06-K2.

elements.text: IT Security Officer
elements.justification: Fills the pattern's 'Risk Officer' role for the query organization; runs the identifier scans and the periodic privacy and AI risk review.

elements.text: Responsible Pharmacist
elements.justification: Adapted from 'Pharmacist in Charge'; in a named-patient supply only the Responsible Pharmacist may authorise disclosure or relocation of a named-patient order record, keeping identifier handling inside a regulated authority.

elements.text: Quality Assurance Officer
elements.justification: Oversight role analogous to the pattern's pharmacy supervision; verifies in the periodic review that privacy controls are documented in the quality system of a regulated distributor.

elements.text: Named-patient orders contain a patient name and a medical record number
elements.justification: Stated in the query; it is the reason G06 needs a separate identifier-containment KPI (G06-K2) in addition to classification, and every proposed element respects it.

elements.text: Hospital staff and patients expect their personal data to be used only for placing, fulfilling and documenting their orders
elements.justification: Adaptation of 'Customers expect data to be used only for their orders'; it justifies demanding a documented purpose for 100% of fields rather than only for sensitive ones.

elements.text: Regulation obliges the distributor to keep traceable records of named-patient supplies, so patient identifiers must exist in the order record and nowhere else
elements.justification: Adapted from 'Regulation requires batch records for every medicine'; it resolves the apparent conflict between minimization and traceability by containing, rather than deleting, identifiers, which is exactly the target of 0 outside the order record.

elements.text: Patient identifiers are never sent to the language model provider, in prompts, retrieval context or logs
elements.justification: Query constraint, mirrored by the pattern constraint on personal data sent to a model provider; it bounds every assistant-related task and is a precondition for G06-K2 reaching 0.

elements.text: Personal data is retained no longer than its documented purpose or its legal retention period requires
elements.justification: The pattern constraint, extended with the regulated retention obligation of the query domain; it makes the retention column of the inventory binding for G06-K1.

elements.text: The identity of the requester is verified before any personal data is released or erased
elements.justification: The pattern constraint applied unchanged; it prevents the deadline pressure of G06-K3 from causing disclosure to the wrong person.

elements.text: Only the Responsible Pharmacist may authorise disclosure or export of a named-patient order record outside the normal fulfilment process
elements.justification: Adapted from 'Only a pharmacist may release quarantined medicines'; it places the most sensitive identifier flows under a single regulated authority and keeps copies from being created ad hoc.

output.rational_statement: G06 serves G01 by making the personal data layer of the regulated order-to-delivery chain controlled in the same way as the product layer: classification with a documented purpose for every field (G06-K1) is the precondition for every later control, because a field whose purpose is unknown can be neither masked, retained correctly, nor kept out of the ordering assistant; containment of patient identifiers inside the named-patient order record (G06-K2) reconciles the belief that such orders must carry a patient name and medical record number with the regulated traceability duty, while the redaction task, the change register and the Responsible Pharmacist authority enforce the constraint that identifiers never reach the language model provider; and the request register with identity verification (G06-K3) turns hospital staff and patient rights into a measurable, deadline-bound service. Together the data inventory, masking tool, identifier exception report and request register give the Data Protection Officer, IT Security Officer, AI Product Owner and Responsible Pharmacist auditable evidence that order-to-delivery is secure and compliant for personal data as well as for medicines.
